summary: The Kohen takes the woman's mincha out of the basket, puts it into a holy kli, and places it on her hand. Then he puts his hand under hers and waves it.

chunks.he: הָיָה נוֹטֵל אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ מִתּוֹךְ כְּפִיפָה מִצְרִית
chunks.en: He would take her mincha out of the Egyptian basket
chunks.st: He would take her meal-offering out of the Egyptian wicker basket made of palm leaves in which it was lying

chunks.en: and put it into a holy kli,
chunks.st: and would put it into a service vessel

chunks.en: and put it on her hand.
chunks.st: and then place it on her hand.

chunks.en: And the Kohen puts his hand under hers and waves it.
chunks.st: And the priest would then place his hand underneath hers and wave it together with her.

summary: The Kohen offers the woman's mincha. The Tanna'im argue whether he first makes her drink the water or first brings the mincha, but either way it is kosher.

chunks.en: He waved it and brought it near (the mizbe'ach),
chunks.st: waved it and brought it near to the southwest corner of the altar,

chunks.en: took a handful and burned it,
chunks.st: removed a handful from it, and burned the handful;

chunks.en: and the rest is eaten by the Kohanim.
chunks.st: and the remainder was eaten by the priests.

chunks.en: He would make her drink, and after that
chunks.st: The priest would force the woman to drink the bitter water of a sota, and afterward

chunks.en: bring her mincha.
chunks.st: he would sacrifice her meal-offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָיָה מַשְׁקָהּ,
chunks.en: He brings her mincha first, and after that he makes her drink,
chunks.st: The priest would sacrifice her meal-offering and afterward he would force her to drink,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And after, he shall make
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And the priest shall take a handful of the meal-offering, as the memorial part of it, and burn it upon the altar,

chunks.en: the woman drink the water."
chunks.st: and afterward he shall make the woman drink the water” (Numbers 5:26).

chunks.en: But if he made her drink first, and after that
chunks.st: But Rabbi Shimon concedes that if the priest first forced her to drink

chunks.en: brought her mincha, it is still kosher.
chunks.st: and afterward sacrificed her meal-offering, it is still valid.

summary: What happens if the woman refuses to drink: before the scroll is erased, she does not have to drink. Once it is erased, she must drink, unless she admits she sinned.

chunks.en: If, before the scroll was erased,
chunks.st: before the scroll was erased

chunks.en: she said, "I will not drink,"
chunks.st: she said: I will not drink,

chunks.en: her scroll is put away,
chunks.st: the scroll that was written for her is sequestered,

words.note: Hidden away, because Hashem's Name is written on it.

chunks.en: and her mincha is scattered on the ash pile.
chunks.st: and her meal-offering is burned and scattered over the place of the ashes,

chunks.en: Her scroll may not be used to make
chunks.st: and her scroll is not fit to give

chunks.en: another sotah drink.
chunks.st: to another sota to drink.

chunks.en: If the scroll was erased and she said, "I am tamei,"
chunks.st: If the scroll was erased and afterward she said: I am defiled,

chunks.he: הַמַּיִם נִשְׁפָּכִין וּמִנְחָתָהּ מִתְפַּזֶּרֶת עַל הַדָּשֶׁן.
chunks.en: the water is spilled out, and her mincha is scattered on the ash pile.
chunks.st: the water is poured out, and her meal-offering is scattered in the place of the ashes.

chunks.en: If the scroll was erased and she said, "I will not drink,"
chunks.st: If the scroll was already erased and she said: I will not drink,

chunks.he: מְעַרְעֲרִים אוֹתָהּ וּמַשְׁקִין אוֹתָהּ בְּעַל כָּרְחָהּ:
chunks.en: they force her to drink, even against her will.
chunks.st: she is forced to drink against her will.

summary: The water shows its power on a guilty woman right away, unless a zechus (merit) holds it off. The Tanna'im also argue about teaching Torah to girls, and list kinds of people who ruin the world.

chunks.he: אֵינָהּ מַסְפֶּקֶת לִשְׁתּוֹת עַד שֶׁפָּנֶיהָ מוֹרִיקוֹת
chunks.en: She does not even finish drinking before her face turns green,
chunks.st: she does not manage to finish drinking before her face turns green

chunks.en: her eyes bulge out, and she fills up with veins,
chunks.st: and her eyes bulge, and her skin becomes full of protruding veins,

chunks.en: and the people say, "Take her out, take her out,
chunks.st: and the people standing in the Temple say: Remove her,

chunks.en: so that she will not make the Azarah tamei."
chunks.st: so that she does not render the Temple courtyard impure
chunks.stMore: by dying there. The mishna limits the scope of the previous statement:

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: If she has a zechus,
chunks.st: If she has merit,

chunks.en: it holds off (the punishment) for her.
chunks.st: it delays punishment for her and she does not die immediately.

chunks.en: Some zechus holds it off for one year,
chunks.st: There is a merit that delays punishment for one year,

chunks.en: some zechus holds it off for two years,
chunks.st: there is a larger merit that delays punishment for two years,

chunks.en: some zechus holds it off for three years.
chunks.st: and there is a merit that delays punishment for three years.

chunks.en: From here Ben Azzai says,
chunks.st: From here Ben Azzai states:

chunks.he: חַיָּב אָדָם לְלַמֵּד אֶת בִּתּוֹ תוֹרָה,
chunks.en: A person must teach his daughter Torah,
chunks.st: A person is obligated to teach his daughter Torah,

chunks.en: so that if she drinks,
chunks.st: so that if she drinks and does not die immediately,

chunks.en: she will know that a zechus is holding it off for her.
chunks.st: she will know that some merit she has delayed punishment for her.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: Anyone who teaches his daughter Torah,
chunks.st: Anyone who teaches his daughter Torah

chunks.en: it is as if he teaches her tiflus (ways that lead to sin).
chunks.st: is teaching her promiscuity [tiflut].

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

chunks.en: A woman would rather have one kav (of food) and be close with her husband
chunks.st: A woman desires to receive the amount of a kav of food and a sexual relationship [tiflut]

chunks.en: than nine kav and be kept apart.
chunks.st: rather than to receive nine kav of food and abstinence.

chunks.en: He used to say,
chunks.st: He would say:

chunks.en: A foolish pious man,
chunks.st: A foolish man of piety,

chunks.en: a sly wicked man,
chunks.st: and a conniving wicked person,

chunks.en: a woman who keeps apart too much,
chunks.st: and an abstinent woman [perusha],

chunks.en: and those who hurt themselves to look holy,
chunks.st: and those who injure themselves out of false abstinence;

words.note: People who act as if they are extra holy.

chunks.en: these people ruin the world.
chunks.st: all these are people who erode the world.

summary: Rabbi Shimon says a zechus does not hold off the water, because then people would doubt the water and the innocent women. Rebbi says it does hold it off, but the woman slowly gets weaker.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: A zechus does not hold off the bitter water.
chunks.st: Merit does not delay the punishment of the bitter water of a sota,

chunks.en: And if you say
chunks.st: and if you say that

chunks.en: that a zechus holds off the water that brings the curse,
chunks.st: merit does delay the punishment of the water that causes the curse, as stated earlier by the Rabbis (20a),

chunks.en: you make the water weak
chunks.st: you weaken [madhe] the power of the bitter water

chunks.en: in the eyes of all the women who drink,
chunks.st: before all the women who drink
chunks.stMore: the water, who will no longer be afraid of it, as they will rely on their merit to save them.

chunks.en: and you give a bad name
chunks.st: And you defame

chunks.en: to the pure women who drank,
chunks.st: the untainted women who drank the water and survived,

chunks.en: since people will say, "They are tamei, but
chunks.st: as people say: They are defiled but

chunks.en: a zechus held it off for them."
chunks.st: it is their merit that delayed the punishment for them.

chunks.en: Rebbi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who put together the Mishnah.

chunks.en: A zechus does hold off the water that brings the curse,
chunks.st: Merit delays the punishment of the water that causes the curse,

chunks.en: but she does not have children and does not grow stronger.
chunks.st: but a woman whose punishment is delayed does not give birth and does not flourish;

chunks.en: Instead, she gets weaker and weaker,
chunks.st: rather, she progressively deteriorates.

chunks.en: and in the end she dies the same death.
chunks.st: Ultimately she dies by the same death as a sota who dies immediately.

summary: If the sotah's mincha becomes tamei, it is treated like any other mincha. The mishnah lists when her mincha must be burned instead of eaten.

chunks.he: נִטְמֵאת מִנְחָתָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָדְשָׁה בַכְּלִי,
chunks.en: If her mincha became tamei before it became holy in the kli,
chunks.st: the meal-offering of the sota is rendered impure before it has been sanctified in the service vessel,

chunks.en: it is like all menachos, and it is redeemed.
chunks.st: its status is like that of all the other meal-offerings that are rendered impure before being sanctified in a service vessel, and it is redeemed.

words.note: Exchanged for money, so it is no longer holy.

chunks.en: But if after it became holy in the kli,
chunks.st: But if it is rendered impure after it has been sanctified in the service vessel,

chunks.en: it is like all menachos, and it is burned.
chunks.st: its status is like that of all the other meal-offerings that are rendered impure after being sanctified in a service vessel, and it is burned.

chunks.en: And these are the women whose menachos are burned:
chunks.st: And these are the sota women whose meal-offerings are burned
chunks.stMore: if they have already been sanctified in a service vessel:

chunks.en: a woman who says, "I am tamei to you,"
chunks.st: A woman who confesses and says: I am defiled, and therefore prohibited to you;

chunks.en: and when witnesses came about her that she is tamei,
chunks.st: and a woman with regard to whom witnesses came and testified that she is defiled;

chunks.en: and one who says, "I will not drink,"
chunks.st: and a woman who says: I will not drink
chunks.stMore: the bitter water of a sota, even if she does not confess her guilt;

chunks.en: and when her husband does not want to make her drink,
chunks.st: and a woman whose husband changed his mind and does not want to force her to drink;

chunks.en: and when her husband was with her as her husband on the way.
chunks.st: and a woman whose husband engaged in sexual intercourse with her on the way to the Temple.

chunks.en: And all women married to Kohanim,
chunks.st: And all the women who are married to priests,

chunks.en: their menachos are burned.
chunks.st: their meal-offerings are always burned,
chunks.stMore: as the verse states: “And every meal-offering of a priest shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten” (Leviticus 6:16).

summary: The mishnah lists ways a Kohen and a Kohen's daughter are different: whose mincha is eaten, who can lose the holiness of kehunah, who may become tamei to the dead, and who eats kodshei kodashim.

chunks.en: A Yisrael woman who married a Kohen,
chunks.st: An Israelite woman who is married to a priest,

chunks.en: her mincha is burned.
chunks.st: her meal-offering is burned;

chunks.en: A Kohen's daughter who married a Yisrael,
chunks.st: and the daughter of a priest who is married to an Israelite,

chunks.en: her mincha is eaten.
chunks.st: her meal-offering is eaten.

chunks.en: What is the difference between a Kohen and a Kohen's daughter?
chunks.st: The mishna asks a general question: What are the differences between a priest and the daughter of a priest?

chunks.en: A Kohen's daughter's mincha is eaten,
chunks.st: The meal-offering of the daughter of a priest is eaten by the priests,

chunks.en: but a Kohen's mincha is not eaten.
chunks.st: but the meal-offering of a priest is not eaten. The

chunks.en: A Kohen's daughter can lose her special holiness,
chunks.st: daughter of a priest can become disqualified
chunks.stMore: from marrying a priest and from partaking of teruma by engaging in sexual intercourse with someone forbidden to her,

chunks.en: but a Kohen does not lose his.
chunks.st: but a priest does not become desacralized
chunks.stMore: by engaging in sexual intercourse with a woman forbidden to him. The

chunks.en: A Kohen's daughter may become tamei to the dead,
chunks.st: daughter of a priest may become impure with impurity imparted by a corpse,

chunks.en: but a Kohen may not become tamei to the dead.
chunks.st: but a priest may not become impure with impurity imparted by a corpse
chunks.stMore: except for the burial of his seven closest relatives.

chunks.en: A Kohen eats kodshei kodashim,
chunks.st: A priest may eat from offerings of the most sacred order,

chunks.en: but a Kohen's daughter does not eat kodshei kodashim.
chunks.st: but the daughter of a priest may not eat from offerings of the most sacred order.

summary: The mishnah lists halachos that are different for a man and for a woman, such as a metzora's mourning signs, nezirus for a child, and punishments of beis din.

chunks.en: What is the difference between a man and a woman?
chunks.st: What are the halakhic differences between a man and a woman?

chunks.en: A man (who is a metzora) lets his hair grow and tears his clothes,
chunks.st: A man lets his hair grow and rends his garments when he is a leper,

chunks.en: but a woman does not let her hair grow or tear her clothes.
chunks.st: but a woman does not let her hair grow or rend her garments when she is a leper.

chunks.en: A man can make his young son a nazir,
chunks.st: A man can vow that his minor son shall be a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: obligating the son to remain a nazirite even during his adulthood,

words.note: A person who promises not to drink wine or cut his hair.

chunks.he: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מַדֶּרֶת אֶת בְּנָהּ בְּנָזִיר.
chunks.en: but a woman cannot make her son a nazir.
chunks.st: but a woman cannot vow that her son shall be a nazirite.

chunks.en: A man can finish his nezirus with his father's nezirus korbanos,
chunks.st: A man can shave at the culmination of his naziriteship by using offerings originally designated for his father’s naziriteship,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if one’s father was also a nazirite and he died having already designated offerings for the culmination of his naziriteship;

chunks.he: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מְגַלַּחַת עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיהָ.
chunks.en: but a woman cannot finish hers with her father's nezirus korbanos.
chunks.st: but a woman cannot shave at the culmination of her naziriteship by using offerings designated for her father’s naziriteship.

chunks.en: A man can sell his young daughter (as a maidservant),
chunks.st: A man can betroth his daughter to another man while she is a minor,

chunks.en: but a woman cannot sell her daughter.
chunks.st: but a woman cannot betroth her daughter even while she is a minor.

chunks.en: A man can give his young daughter in marriage,
chunks.st: A man can sell his daughter as a maidservant while she is a minor,

chunks.en: but a woman cannot give her daughter in marriage.
chunks.st: but a woman cannot sell her daughter as a maidservant even while she is a minor.

chunks.en: A man is stoned without his clothes,
chunks.st: A man is stoned naked,

chunks.en: but a woman is not stoned without her clothes.
chunks.st: but a woman is not stoned naked.

chunks.en: A man is hung (after being stoned),
chunks.st: A man is hanged
chunks.stMore: after he is stoned for certain transgressions,

chunks.en: but a woman is not hung.
chunks.st: but a woman is not hanged.

chunks.en: A man is sold (as a servant) for his stealing,
chunks.st: A man is sold for his committing an act of theft in order to pay his debt,

chunks.en: but a woman is not sold for her stealing.
chunks.st: but a woman is not sold for her committing an act of theft.
